ParlaMint-RS_2013-11-04-0.u25511	Dear Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, at the beginning of today's debate, allow me in principle to make a few preliminary remarks on the draft law on the seats and areas of courts and public prosecutors, the draft law amending and supplementing the Law on the regulation of courts, the draft law amending and supplementing the Law on Judges and the Proposal for a Law on Amendments and Supplements to the Law on the Public Prosecutor's Office. First of all, I would like to remind you that the National Assembly recently adopted a new National Strategy for Justice Reform for the period from 2013 to 2018, and that the government soon thereafter adopted the Action Plan for the implementation of the National Strategy. The draft laws we will discuss today in the National Assembly represent only the first step in achieving the objectives set out in the new National Strategy, and above all improving the work and efficiency of the judiciary, better access to the court, increasing citizens' confidence in the work of the judicial authorities. The four draft laws were prepared following a detailed analysis of the existing situation in the justice of the Republic of Serbia, after which working groups consisted of representatives of all stages of the courts and public prosecutors, as well as representatives of law schools, lawyers, associations of judges and public prosecutors, as well as meetings of working groups were attended by representatives of international organisations. The working texts of the draft law were carried out by a comprehensive public debate in which all interested parties could declare the proposed solutions. I remind you there's been an organized public hearing at the National Assembly. I will also note that the proposed laws were already in the assembly procedure in almost identical text as early as April 2013, but were withdrawn due to certain minor changes made to improve the text of the bill. After consultations were carried out both with the professional public and with the representatives of the European Commission, draft laws were submitted for consideration and adoption to the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia. I will also point out that all these four draft laws represent in fact one continent, given that the solutions made by each individual law are interrelated to the solutions proposed in other laws. First, I will present the draft law on the seats and areas of the courts and public prosecutors. The reason for the adoption of a new law, rather than amending an existing law, is that a number of shortcomings related to the territorial organisation of courts and public prosecutors have been observed in relation to the current law. The biggest lack of current law is seen in the fact that there are only 34 basic courts in the Republic of Serbia, within them a large number of judicial units. Since the basic courts, as the name itself says, form the basis of the judicial system in the Republic of Serbia and that the majority of citizens appear as parties to the proceedings before those courts, the existing territorial organisation of the basic courts did not allow citizens an effective approach to the court, so it was necessary to change the existing solution thoroughly. The analysis of the work of the courts has shown that it is necessary to increase the number of basic courts to 66, as well as to reduce the number of judicial units at the same time since they have proved to be a irrational solution. In addition, with the aim of more effective work of the Public Prosecutor's Office, which primarily refers to the prosecution of perpetrators, and given the fact that it has begun the application of the new Code of Criminal Procedure under which the Public Prosecutor's Office plays a much more active role in the proceedings, the number of basics has increased, public prosecutors to 58 in this draft law. When it comes to criminal courts, the existing territorial organisation of these courts has not been changed. In view of the existing legal solutions, we believe that there are still 44 misdemeanor courts in line with our needs for the effective conduct of the infringement procedure, although the working group has also made a proposal to amend the network of criminal courts. As I have already pointed out, the most important newspaper provided for by the bill concerns the arrangement of the seat and the area of jurisdiction of the basic courts. The proposed network of 66 basic courts is based on analysis of the work of basic courts, the average annual inflow of cases, the criteria of geographical distance, the development of the travel network, the number of inhabitants, sometimes tradition, as well as the real needs of citizens for judicial protection. At the same time, a reduction in the number of judicial units was made, since they did not justify the reasons why they were educated, which is, above all, the approach of the citizens to the court, while on the other hand, they caused major costs in the functioning of the basic courts. In view of the fact that a judicial profession has been established, the establishment of a judicial profession and a public register, which should take over the responsibilities of partial and basic courts, is, above all, in a non-partisan procedure, which should start with the work of 1 October 2014, a transitional solution to the draft law provides for still existing judicial units in place in places in which there are still legal units, whose abolition is proposed, to educate the reception offices that will carry out the tasks of admission of documents, certification of documents and signatures, and in order to enable citizens to have easier access to the court during this transitional period. I would not be kept for longer on the statistical data which are in favour of the proposed network of basic courts, since the draft law also provides a detailed analysis of the effects of the law containing these data. Only as an illustration of the irrationality of the existing network of basic courts will I give an example of the Second Basic Court in Belgrade, which covers the territory of the so-called so-called Court of Justice. Belgrade suburban municipalities, which is quite dissociated and with a large number of inhabitants, resulting in the court having the highest burden on the inflow of new cases, and new cases by judge, which is more than twice as much as the court that had the least burden. Instead of that court, the bill provides for the establishment of three basic courts in Lazarovac, Obrenovac and Mladenov, which will only have a judicial unit in Sopot. When it comes to senior courts, an existing solution to their number has been retained. And as for the territory they cover, it is in line with the solutions set out in the draft laws governing the jurisdiction of primary courts and senior courts in the Republic of Serbia. The draft law has not changed the territorial organisation of economic courts, nor has the number of departments of the Criminal, Appealal and Administrative Court. In relation to the existing Law, significant changes have been made in respect of the areas of jurisdiction of the Courts of Appeal, which corrects the irrational solutions contained in the applicable law. Under the current law, the Belgrade Court of Appeal is responsible, among other things, for the areas of senior courts in Zajecar and Negotin. Such a solution certainly is not rational, because these cities are much closer to Nis than Belgrade, which is why the bill provides for the area of these courts to be competent for the Court of Appeal in Nis. Because Negotin is 238 km away from Belgrade and from Nis 152 km away, while Zaječar is 246 km away from Belgrade and Nis only 95 km away, for the same reasons, the territorial jurisdiction of the Court of Appeal in Belgrade and for the area of the Higher Court in Pancheva is foreseen. When it comes to the territorial organisation of public prosecutors, the solutions set out in the bill are mostly accompanied by a territorial organisation of courts. As has been said, the number of basic public prosecutors has increased from the existing 34 to the new 58th. The number of basic prosecutors is lower than the number of basic courts, for rationality reasons. Therefore, the bill provides for eight public prosecutors to cover the area of two basic courts, namely – the General Public Prosecutor's Office in Vranj, and for the Court of Justice in Bujanovac, the General Public Prosecutor's Office in Zajecar and for the Area of the Basic Court in Književec, the General Public Prosecutor's Office in Negotin and for the Main Court in Majdanpek, the General Public Prosecutor's Office in Novi Pazar and for the Area of the Basic Court in Sjenica, the General Public Prosecutor's Office in Piroth and the District Court in Dimitrovgrad, the General Public Prosecutor's Office in Prijepo and the General Court in Priboj, the General Public Prosecutor's Office in Sremska Mitrovica and the Main Court in Šid and the General Public Prosecutor's Office in Cacca and for the Main Court in Ivanjicja. I particularly highlight the provision of Article 12. A bill that provides for special legislation to regulate the seats and areas of courts and public prosecutors responsible for the territory of the AP Kosovo and Metohija. This solution is in line with all measures so far taken by the Government, on the one hand, and on the other hand, safeguards the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Republic of Serbia in the event that the provisions of the concluded agreements concerning the organisation of judicial authorities in the territory of the AP Kosovo and Metohija are not implemented. The transitional provisions of the bill set out the continuation of the work of existing courts and public prosecutors until the start of the application of the law, the way in which the cases were taken over, as well as the transfer of judges and deputy public prosecutors, i.e. the appointment of the perpetrators of the presidents of the courts and public prosecutors in newly established courts and public prosecutors. The application of the law is scheduled for 1 January 2014, in order to implement the necessary technical and organisational preparations for its application by that date. Allow me to make a few preliminary remarks on the draft law on amendments and additions to the Law on the Regulation of Courts. The proposed solutions should be observed in relation to the solutions set out in the Bill on Seats and Areas of Courts and Public Prosecutors. The most significant amendments to the Law on the Regulation of Courts relate to the change in jurisdiction of the basic and senior courts. Another significant paper contained in the draft law is the regulation of a special procedure for the protection of the right to trial within a reasonable period of time, which will be decided under the judicial system, and not as prescribed by the applicable laws, that the only legal means that the party is entitled to submit a constitutional appeal for trial within a reasonable period of time. I note that the text of the working version of the law, as well as the other laws that are now on the agenda, has been provided with expertise from the Venice Commission of the Council of Europe and that observations from expertise have been incorporated into the proposed texts. As I have pointed out, the special paper is a regulation of the procedure for the protection of the right to trial within a reasonable period of time. The provisions of the draft law give the possibility to a party who considers that it has been violated the right to trial within a reasonable period of time, to refer to a higher court, with a request for protection of the right to trial within a reasonable period of time. By deciding on the party's request, a directly senior court, if it considers that the application is justified, may set a lower court deadline within which it is required to end the proceedings, and may also set a temporary compensation for the violation of the right to trial within a reasonable period of time, which shall be paid out of the budget. Against a negative decision, directly to the senior court, at the request of the party, a complaint can be made to the Supreme Cassation Court. This strengthens the protection of the right to trial within the judicial system of the Republic of Serbia, which will, on the one hand, increase the discipline in the work of the courts and, on the other hand, certainly reduce the number of constitutional complaints filed, the Constitutional Court, as well as the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg. The paper in the draft law also provides the solution that trials are held in the judicial unit for the entire territory of the court in certain court proceedings, i.e. matter in accordance with the annual court schedule. Such a solution, together with the solutions set out in the Bill on Seats and Areas of Courts and Public Prosecutors, will contribute to the more efficient work of courts and the reduction of judicial costs, as well as the costs of participants in the process. With regard to the jurisdiction of the courts, the bill extends the first-degree jurisdiction of the High Court for all crimes against humanity and other goods protected by international law, as well as for the most difficult forms of new criminal acts of corruption. In addition, the jurisdiction of the High Court and of the trial in the second instance is extended by establishing the jurisdiction of the High Court to decide on complaints against decisions of the basic courts on all measures to ensure the presence of the accused, as well as criminal offences for which a sentence of up to five years is threatened. In this way, a different distribution of real jurisdiction between basic and higher courts will be carried out, resulting in the discharge of the basic courts. Given that the largest number of court proceedings ends before the appeals courts, and since there are four appeals courts in the Republic of Serbia, the issue of inequality of court decisions has arisen in practice when handled in similar or similar legal situations. Given that a large number of procedures do not provide for the possibility of investing in an emergency legal remedy decided by the Supreme Cassation Court, which, through a decision on those legal remedies, would balance judicial practice, it is necessary to establish a mechanism to overcome this problem. That is why the bill provides for appeals courts to hold joint meetings and inform the Supreme Cassation Court about issues of issue of importance for the functioning of courts in the Republic of Serbia and the harmonisation of case law. This supplement is of paramount importance for the equal treatment of courts in the same legal matters in the Republic of Serbia, which is very important for the equality of all citizens before the law, and this will also contribute to a reduction of the number of constitutional complaints, i.e. performances before the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg. One of the EU's most important recommendations in the accession process was the specialisation of courts for trial in copyright and related rights disputes. In this respect, the draft law provides for exclusive jurisdiction of the economic courts for the trial in these disputes, regardless of whether economic operators or natural persons appear as parties. In addition, since the proposal for a law on the seats and areas of courts and public prosecutors provides for the jurisdiction of the Belgrade Chamber of Commerce to act in the first instance in copyright and related rights disputes, both specialisation and concentration of jurisdiction are possible, thus fulfilling the EU's recommendations. The draft law amends the name of the High Court of Violation in the Criminal Court of Appeal, and given that that court has exclusive second-degree jurisdiction and that its name is aligned with the names of other courts with exclusive second-degree jurisdiction, such as the Court of Appeal and the Court of Appeal. The jurisdiction of the Supreme Cassation Court has been deleted to establish the principle of legal views for the sake of uniform judicial application of law, given that the Constitution of the Republic of Serbia does not know the principal legal views of the Supreme Cassation Court as a source of law on the basis of which judicial decisions are taken, instead it is prescribed that the Supreme Court provides for a uniform judicial application of the rights and equality of parties in the court proceedings. The bill provides for the possibility that special services for assistance and support for witnesses and injured persons, which, according to applicable regulations, exist only in war crimes proceedings, are being educated in the context of the cases of the judicial administration. The proposed solutions are moving forward with a tendency in the modern laws of the European countries where there are special services to support and assist witnesses and damage to the trial in criminal matters in which they may appear, especially for the crimes of organised crime and crimes with elements of violence. In order to make the court's work more efficient and discharging the President of the Court, it is predicted that all courts of the Republic rank, as well as courts with more than 30 judges, must have a manager, not as so far as the court's manager, who performs material financial and organisational technical affairs in the court. The draft law lays down the right for judges to be able to make an insight into their personal list, as well as to object to its content, thus harmonising with the Personal Data Protection Act. In order to strengthen the independence of the judicial authority, and in accordance with the national strategy of judicial reform and recommendations of the Venice Commission and the European Commission, the draft law lays down a deadline for the transfer of jurisdiction from the Ministry of Justice and the State Administration to the VSS, with a view to establishing the criteria for determining the number of judicial staff, the conduct of the affairs of the judicial administration, as well as the adoption and exercise of supervision over the application of the Rules of Procedure. In addition, a deadline has been set for the termination of the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Justice and of the State Administration in relation to giving an opinion on a VSS act proposing the scope and structure of budgetary resources for the ongoing expenditure of judicial authorities, as well as for the supervision of the expenditure of the budget funds identified for the work of courts. It is proposed to assume those responsibilities by the VSS as of 1 June 2016, in order to create the necessary human and technical conditions for the takeover of these responsibilities. In view of the fact that the bill changes certain competences, primarily basic and senior courts, the law is intended to start to apply on 1 January 2014, at the same time as the application of the law on seats and areas of courts and public prosecutors. In short, I would point out the most significant solutions to the Bill of Amendments and Supplements of the Law on Judges which occurred because of the need for individual provisions of the law, and in particular provisions relating to the independence of the judge, to move and refer the judge to another court, to the public in the choice of judges and president of the courts, as well as the provisions on disciplinary responsibility, to specify and supplement. The draft law sets out the provisions governing the institution of the transfer of judges, in the light of constitutional provisions guaranteeing the unmovableness of the judge, the draft law provides for the notion of a change in the court's prerogatives, as a reason for the Judge's transfer to another court, without its own consent. It is also prescribed that the judge in this case may be transferred only to the court of the same degree that assumes the jurisdiction of the suspended court, which means that he cannot be transferred by the judge from Subotica to, for example, the basic court in Leskovec, Vranja or Piroth, but exclusively in the area of the basic court in Subotica. Taking into account the importance of the right to a natural judge, the draft law provides for more precise arrangements for derogations from the order of admission of cases, as well as cases where a judge may be seized and assigned to another judge. That provision shall allow, in addition to the protection of the right to a natural judge and the security of the right to trial within a reasonable period of time, in the event that the judge is absent for a long time or if there are other reasons why the case is not being handled. The proposed law amends the provisions of the Law on Judges which regulate the evaluation of the work of judges and the President of courts. It is proposed that the work of the judges and the president of the courts be valued by the VSS committees. The Commission will have three members, with judges of the higher level to evaluate the work of a lower-level judge, taking into account their long-term work experience at the judge's office, as well as the possibility of insight into the work of lower-level judges. Against the judge's assessment, it has the right to object, which is decided by a special commission of the VSS composed exclusively of judges of the Supreme Court of Cassation. A legal protection which can be achieved in the administrative dispute before the administrative court has been provided against the decision on the objection. The bill provides for the obligation to hold talks with candidates who are first elected to a judicial post, not only the possibility as provided for so far. In addition, in order to bring the law into line with law under the Judicial Academy, the High Council of the Judiciary is required to propose a candidate who completed his initial training at the Judicial Academy when proposing candidates for the election. Such a solution is foreseen for the selection of judges of the criminal or basic court, i.e. the courts of the lowest degree. With regard to the provisions of the Law on Judges, concerning the President of the Court, it is predicted as a new condition that only a judge who is in permanent judicial office may be elected for the President of the Court in order to avoid the possibility of a judge first elected as judge. In addition, it has been proposed that the High Council of the Judiciary for the President of the Court, instead of more candidates, propose one candidate. Such a solution is more appropriate compared to a valid legal solution, given that the procedure before the High Council of the Court provides for a detailed procedure allowing the High Judicial Council to propose the best candidate for the President-in-Office. It predicts that the term of office of the President of the Court takes five years instead of four years, which is the same solution that the Constitution prescribes for the President of the Supreme Cassation Court. In accordance with the constitutional provision, as well as for the President of the Supreme Cassation Court, the same person is expected to be elected once as President of the Court. The bill shortened the time set by the court president's office from one year to six months, and given that it was an emergency situation, it is necessary to select the president as soon as possible. When it comes to selecting the President of the Supreme Cassation Court, the Law on Judges is complemented in order to ensure public insight on the quality of candidates data, with information on candidates being provided on the website of the High Council of Justice. It provides that candidates are required to deliver an appropriate programme to improve the work of the judicial system in the Republic of Serbia. The bill explicitly prohibits jury judges from being members of political parties, i.e. to participate in political activities, which is significant for impartial decision-making in court proceedings. In this way, judges are leveled with professional judges, when it comes to banning political action. The significant newspapers represent amendments to the provisions relating to the disciplinary procedure. It is envisaged that certain disciplinary penalties can be imposed each and every one, but also cumulatively, allowing more disciplinary sanctions to be imposed in any particular case. Also, the length of limitation periods for the conduct of disciplinary proceedings has been changed from one to two years since the date of the disciplinary offence was committed, given that even more complicated disciplinary offences can occur, which may lead to a longer disciplinary procedure. At the same time, additional legal protection is foreseen in the disciplinary proceedings against judges, so that the judge can file a complaint in the administrative dispute against a second-degree disciplinary decision. I'll introduce you to the amendments to the Law on Amendments and Supplements to the Law on Public Prosecutor's Office. In the course of the application of the Law on the Public Prosecutor's Office, certain provisions, in particular provisions relating to the organisation of the work of the Public Prosecutor's Office, the hierarchical relationship between the public prosecutor's office holders, the rules on the selection of deputy public prosecutor, the procedure for the selection of public prosecutors and the deputy public prosecutor's office, the evaluation of the work and the deputy public prosecutor's office, as well as the provisions on disciplinary responsibility should be specified and complemented. The bill provides for the possibility that the basic public prosecutor's office can also be established for several basic courts, which is in line with the proposal for a law on seats and areas of courts and public prosecutors, which provides for eight public prosecutors to be established for the area of two basic courts. In addition, it envisions the possibility that other public prosecutors, not only the public prosecutor's office, may have departments outside their seats. In this way, it is possible that, if there are no necessary conditions for the establishment of a public prosecutor's office, such a public prosecutor's office is not established, but that the department of the already existing public prosecutor's office is educated. The provisions of the Law on the Public Prosecutor's Office have been amended to regulate the issuing of mandatory instructions directly by the senior public prosecutor to the lower public prosecutor. In this way, when it is necessary to take action, which does not suffer a delay, an exception is provided in relation to the rule that the mandatory instruction must be in writing. In this respect, a directly senior public prosecutor shall be obliged to deliver this instruction in writing within three days. With this exception, whose need for regulation has been shown by practice, it allows for more effective work by the prosecution, where the obligation to issue instructions in writing, as a basic rule, is not violated. An identical solution concerns the issuing of a mandatory public prosecutor's instructions to his deputy. The bill stipulates that a republican public prosecutor has an obligation to submit a regular annual report on the work of public prosecutors in the Republic of Serbia to the National Assembly. In this way, it is possible for a body choosing and deciding to suspend the role of the republican public prosecutor, through regular annual reports, to have insight into the work of public prosecutors in the Republic of Serbia. In view of the solutions set out in the Bill on Seats and Areas of Courts and Public Prosecutors, it is necessary to specify the concept of abolishing the Public Prosecutor's Office. It is predicted that the public prosecutor's office is suspended in the case where the area of jurisdiction is divided into two or more public prosecutors. In this proposal for a law, it was agreed with the Law on the Judicial Academy, provided that the State's Chief Prosecutors were obliged to propose a candidate who had completed training at the Academy when proposing candidates for the selection of a deputy public prosecutor. The bill envisions the obligation to hold talks with candidates who are elected to the public prosecutor's office. In this way, it is possible for the applicant reported to present further clarifications in the interview with the members of the State Council of Prosecutors and to provide additional information that is relevant for the selection of candidates. This ensures greater transparency in the selection process for candidates. To the greater public in the process of electing candidates to the public prosecutor's office, it is envisaged that the State's major prosecutors, when proposing and electing candidates, have the obligation to draw up a ranking list based on pre-arranged criteria and criteria and which must be publicly published on the State's Council of Prosecutors' website. As in the Proposal for a Law on Amendments and Supplements to the Law on Judges, an amendment has been made to the length of the limitation period for the conduct of a disciplinary procedure from one to two years from the date of the disciplinary offence committed, and given that even more complex disciplinary offences can occur which may lead to a longer disciplinary procedure. The possibility of a administrative dispute against a second-degree disciplinary decision is also foreseen. In the shortest lines, this would be the most significant newspaper in these draft laws. Let me thank you at the end of this initial presentation for your attention and express my hope that, after the debate in principle and in particular, the proposed laws will be adopted, creating conditions for achieving the objectives set out in the National Strategy for Justice Reform, while contributing to greater legal certainty and more effective protection of the rights of citizens and economic operators in the Republic of Serbia. Thank you for your attention.

ParlaMint-RS_2013-11-04-0.u25529	The President-in-Office, representatives of the ministry, respected colleagues and colleagues, as today we will discuss in the joint principle debate the draft law on seats and areas of courts, public prosecutors, the draft law amending and supplementing the Law on Courts, the draft law amending and supplementing the Law on Public Prosecutors, the fact that the Constitution of the Republic of Serbia requires the establishment, organisation, jurisdiction, regulation and assembly of courts to be governed by the law, and that is the reason for these proposals to be found before the parliament of the Republic of Serbia. Of course, this matter has previously been regulated by law, but during their application certain normative shortcomings, which consisted of inadequate territorial organisation, have been inadequately divided by jurisdiction between basic and higher courts, from inequality of practice, which is all leading to problems in the functioning of courts and the exercise of the rights of citizens, in particular to a fair trial, i.e. a reasonable trial, as fundamental human rights, which are guaranteed by the European Convention on Human Rights and which are entitled to democratic societies. As this matter is divided into four different but mutually complementary laws, we will speak individually of each of these laws. The draft law on the seats and areas of courts and public prosecutors, the applicable law has been implemented since 1 January 2010 and only 34 basic courts and a large number of judicial units are currently in place under this legal solution in Serbia, 102 of them. The number was replaced by a previous number of 138 municipal courts. It has been observed that such a solution is inadequate and that it would be celery to increase the number of courts to 66 and reduce judicial units. This proposal is based on an analysis of work so far, on the annual inflow of cases and on the need to make the judicial authority more accessible to the public in order to achieve full, effective protection of rights. A large number of judicial units, among other things, have led to ineffectiveness, cost increases, as many proceedings have been conducted outside the court's seat, showing overall insufficient capacity, with the security risk of permanent transfer of court files outside the court building. The existing network of courts and public prosecutors has proved to be dysfunctional, expensive, with the unequal burden of courts and judges, public prosecutors and their deputies, which in itself leads to an unequal approach to courts, i.e. justice, inequalities of citizens and parties, legal uncertainty and ineffectiveness, as well as in major labour shortages, and in an unwarranted length of judicial proceedings, which can also be considered a legal and political problem. To solve these problems, i.e. In order to contribute more effectively to the work of courts, not only must the network be improved, but it is also necessary to implement and implement other laws, not only contained in this set of laws, but also those which, according to their matter, also improve the work of courts and relieve citizens of major problems so far, which are the Law on Public Records, the Law on Enforcement and Security, the Law on Free Legal Assistance, which will particularly affect the removal of some of the jurisdiction of the basic courts from the courts themselves, which would be in the interest of citizens. One of the legal solutions of the Belgrade court's network as the capital is that instead of the two basic courts so far, the First and Second Court, with four judicial units, six courts are established, the First, the Second and the Third Basic Court and the basic courts in Lazarovac, Obrenovac and Mladenov with the judicial unit in Sopot. A similar solution was given to the prosecutor's network, just as it was given to the courts. The change of the network of courts involves the establishment of new courts, as well as the change of the area, i.e. territory for certain multiple courts. For example, the Supreme Court in Belgrade has the area of six Belgrade basic courts, as well as the area of jurisdiction of the appeals courts, which also extends territorial jurisdiction over the one established by the existing law. The aim of this law certainly is to establish an effective, efficient, modern and economic judiciary, in order to achieve the right to access justice, an effective solution to the problem of citizens and businesses with as little cost as possible, with rapid decision-making in the interests of society as a whole. The right to trial within a reasonable period of time and the right of the party in a court procedure to decide its rights without undue delay, this right is guaranteed by the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights, which the Republic of Serbia has ratified, thus accepting the obligation to respect that same right. As regards the draft law amending and supplementing the Law on Courts, the applicable law was passed in 2008 and application began on 1 January 2010. In its application, the existing law showed a number of shortcomings, primarily in the division of jurisdiction between primary and senior courts, the inequality of judicial practice in the proceedings of the Court of Appeal, which in total with an inadequate network of courts has contributed to a major problem in the functioning of courts and the exercise of citizens' rights to trial within a reasonable period of time. Legislative solutions proposed by a better legal framework to improve judicial practice and for more effective trials, the solutions proposed so far have effects on all courts. It is the High Council of the judiciary, the Ministry of Justice, the citizens and legal persons. The jurisdiction of the senior court in the first degree is extended for all crimes against humanity and other goods protected by international law, as well as for the crime of corruption, regardless of the threatened sentence. The jurisdiction of this court shall be extended to decide by appeal against decisions of the basic courts in all measures to ensure the presence of the accused, e.g. which is a detention, as well as for crimes for which a sentence of up to five years has been threatened. The jurisdiction of economic courts is extended to the regulation of copyright and related rights and other rights relating to this matter, by exempting from their jurisdiction the conduct of proceedings in disputes relating to liquidation and bankruptcy. With regard to the jurisdiction of the criminal and second-degree criminal court, it shall be governed by the jurisdiction of the criminal appeal court in the second instance, which shall be brought by the authorities of the administration in the criminal proceedings, which falls within the jurisdiction of the criminal court. It also extends the jurisdiction of the administrative court to provide international legal assistance under its jurisdiction. A significant paper prescribed by these provisions is in the provision of Article 2 where Articles 8a to 8b are added, which provides for the possibility for parties who are considered to have been injured by the right to trial within a reasonable period of time to address a directly higher court with a request for protection of the right of trial within a reasonable period, and would, in accordance with the proposed solution, be directly superior to the court, if it considers that such a request is justified, set a lower court within which it is required to complete the proceedings, and may also provide for a temporary compensation for the infringement of the right paid out of the budget. If a senior court finds that such a request is unjustified, a negative decision shall be taken, the possibility of appeal shall be allowed to the Supreme Cassation Court. The idea of the legislator is to increase judicial discipline and reduce the number of constitutional complaints filed by the Constitutional Court, as well as the number of representations to the European Court of Human Rights. At this point, however, citizens and the professional public face a kind of dilemma about their ability to exercise the rights guaranteed by the Serbian Constitution. Serbia's constitution envisioned the possibility of submitting constitutional appeal as means of legal protection not only of those human rights guaranteed by the Constitution, but also of those rights guaranteed and arising from the European Convention on the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms. Namely, the constitutional appeal represents a very effective remedy within the legal system and is a prerequisite for citizens of Serbia to make up and be able to present before the European Court of Human Rights. From the legal options offered by this law, and as mentioned above, it is possible to refer directly to a higher court in the event of a breach of the right of trial within a reasonable period of time, it is not precisely stated whether the citizens who believe that they have been violated by the Constitution remain in a parallel position to make a constitutional appeal with the possibility offered by this legal solution or are lost in the future, since the Constitutional Court protects human rights in cases where the possibility of judicial or other protection is not provided for under the Constitution of guaranteed rights, including the right to be tried within a reasonable period of time. If such a legal solution is a way of improving the position of the Republic of Serbia before the European Court of Justice, to reduce the damage in this regard to reducing the number of performances, then the proposed legislative solution should be accepted. The proposal for this law and extending the jurisdiction of individual courts and organisational changes would reduce the number of old cases since the analyses show the highest number of cases in basic courts. Some newspaper of laws such as the introduction of the governor of courts, a more rational relationship with complaints of citizens, professionalisation of the work of judicial assistants and the transition of the ministry's jurisdiction to the High Council of the judiciary are in any case signs of modernisation and new perceptions of the rule of law. The draft law amending and supplementing the Law on Judges, the applicable law adopted in 2008, which has been applied since 2010, regulates the position of judges, the procedure for their election, the termination of judicial functions and the reasons for resolution, the position of jury judges and the disciplinary responsibility of judges. Since the practice pointed out that the provisions relating to the independence of judges, as well as other principles guaranteeing its position, referring to work in another court, the provisions on disciplinary responsibility, are not sufficiently precise and have been approached by amendments. We're going to talk about the most important thing now to improve the work of the judiciary as a whole. Of course, attention should be paid to the provisions relating to the responsibility of the judge for the damage caused by illegal or irregular work. Namely, when a decision of the Constitutional Court, the European Court of Human Rights or another international court finds that human rights and fundamental freedoms have been violated in the course of the proceedings or that the judgment has failed because of the violation of the right to trial within a reasonable period of time, the judge will be responsible for the damage only if it has been done on purpose, leaving out the possibility of collecting damage caused by extreme negligence. The provisions of Articles 11 and 12 now uniformly regulate the evaluation of judges and presidents, and the evaluation of judges is entrusted to the Commission of the High Council of the judiciary in which judges and members of the Commission will evaluate the work of a lower-level judge, since they also have longer working experience in the judicial capacity and because of the possibility of direct insight into the work of lower-degree judges. In the event of disagreement, there is the possibility of objecting and the possibility of conducting a administrative dispute. The decision on the termination of the judicial post must be reasoned, which has not been prescribed so far, and the discharge procedure shall be initiated on official duty or on a proposal from other persons and other bodies. The bill limits the time it can be set to serve as acting President of the Court and will set shorter deadlines for the duration of this situation. A significant newspaper refers to Article 100 in the political party, political action, and is limited in this respect to the right for the judge of the jury and these rights for judges are identical, as well as to restrictions relating to judges. The provision of Article 30 of the Law provides for provisions relating to serious disciplinary offences that are being resolved by the judge, such as the limitation of the case being considered a serious disciplinary offence if it is found to be an unconscious act of the judge, unless there are circumstances that the judge cannot influence, when the case is physically not in his jurisdiction. The objective of these amendments is to consistently implement constitutional provisions governing the position of the judge and compliance with international standards. So, one necessary legal framework is given to improve the work of the judiciary in general, to make it effective, efficient and modern with a reduction of the accumulated deficits. In view of the scope and content of the amendments, of which only the most important ones are mentioned, we believe that the law will act positively on judges in the judiciary system in general, including the High Council of the judiciary as an independent and independent body guaranteeing the independence and independence of courts and judges in relation to other participants in the process and society in general. The draft law amending and supplementing the Law on the Public Prosecutor's Office, since practice has shown that certain provisions of the applicable law relating to the independence of the public prosecutor, the hierarchical relationship of the prosecutor's office, the duration of the election and evaluation procedure, should be specified and complemented by international standards. That's exactly what this bill does. The bill also provides for the public prosecutor's duty to carry out his duties professionally, securely, impartially, fairly and without undue delay, with the obligation to take special care of the protection of the damaged, as well as to prevent discrimination on any basis. The new law allows a public prosecutor's office to cover the area of higher basic courts, which is in line with the principles of rationality. The mandatory instruction given by a directly senior public prosecutor must be in writing, and it is the obligation of the public prosecutor to reject any action that affects the independence of the public prosecutor, which strengthens one of the basic principles, the principle of independence of the function. A significant change relates to the election procedure for the public prosecutor's office, and predicts that the State's major prosecutors may, when proposing an election, draw up a ranking list of candidates on the basis of the pre-determined criteria, published on the internet, while the discharge procedure may be made public if it is requested by the public prosecutor against whom the proceedings are being conducted. Based on everything that has been stated so far, we can conclude that on the basis of the proposed amendments and additions to the laws that lie ahead of us today, justice in Serbia could be made available, effective, independent in all parts of the country, correcting the mistakes made by creating a new network of courts, identifying the problems facing courts and prosecutors, especially those facing Serbian citizens. We think that the proposed set of law in the area of the judiciary is a response to the perceived problems, that it will certainly contribute to the overall legislative and judicial reform, as well as to the European integration of the Republic of Serbia. Based on what has been said, we point out that the SDPS will support the proposed laws in the voting day.

ParlaMint-RS_2013-11-04-0.u25690	Dear Mr. President, the Honorable Presidency, the ladies and gentlemen of the People's Parliament, I always feel great satisfaction and great responsibility and willingness to accept everything that you as MPs think is useful and necessary to use in the documents we are talking about today in the field of traffic with special pleasure. I'm undermining again. I'm always leaving this high house to learn something new. A lot of people here know a lot about traffic, and that's why I'd like to thank you in advance for the suggestions you're about to make. In short, I will explain all three proposals for the document. The first is the draft law on railways. The main objectives of this law are to improve the efficiency of the Republika Srpska rail system, integrate it into the transport services market and integrate Serbian rail into the EU rail system. The adoption of this bill will bring national legislation into line with EU rules, which is a key priority in the EU accession process and implementing European rules on the area of rail transport. The proposal for a railway law shall further develop the relationship between the state and its authorities and the railway companies as their responsibilities, obligations and conditions to be met by railway companies in order to carry out the work for which they are established. It is regulated to separate the railway system to the part relating to the management of railway infrastructure, the organisation and regulation of the transport of management infrastructure and to the part relating to passenger and freight transport, the railway undertaking and their operations, which means their specific financing. The creation of conditions for the emergence of several railway undertakings, which should lead to competition and increased transport quality, as well as the liberalisation of the railway market. It is also foreseen by the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia to adopt a five-year national programme of railway infrastructure on a proposal from the Government of Serbia, which determines the state of existing infrastructure, building plans, reconstruction and maintenance of infrastructure, determines the tasks, their scope, dynamics, realisation and priorities, heights and sources of financial resources needed for the realisation of the national programme, defining the obligations of infrastructure managers, which their annual plans must comply with the national programme. The proposal for a railway law sets out more precisely the provisions defined for a public transport obligation, whose services are needed and applied in EU countries, and for reasons of general economic interest cannot currently be provided on a commercial basis. The purpose of the provisions relating to the public transport obligation is to prescribe the conduct of state authorities, AP authorities and local law enforcement authorities, on the one hand, as well as railway undertakings, on the other hand, in the field of public transport of passengers, and in order to ensure the provision of services of general interest, which are, among other things, better quality or at lower prices than those which would be possible solely on the basis of the functioning of market laws. Special attention is paid to the regulation of combined transport, where most of the transport route is carried out by rail, which, despite its importance and potentials, is largely neglected in the current Railway Act. Also, this law provides for the possibility of stimulating combined transport. This law also defines more precisely the responsibilities and tasks of the Railway Directorate, which according to European regulations and standards should be represented by the licensing body, the regulatory body and the safety body. The draft law on railways provides the basis for the initial phase of the rail system restructuring process in the Republic of Serbia. The activities are under way to restructure Serbia's Railways and, according to the plans of the Ministry of Transport, it is envisaged that the future organisational structure consists of four dependent companies within the group of companies, such as: a public railway infrastructure management company, a public transport company for public transport of passengers in rail transport and maintenance of railway vehicles in this type of transport, a public transport service company, a public transport service company in railway transport and maintenance of railway trains, vehicles in this type of transport and a company for the operation of real estate management and other property of the railways of Serbia. In this way, the organisation and functioning of subsidiaries would be consistent with the location of income, and financial and business independence would exist by segments. The process of reforms and investment activities undertaken by the Government of the Republic of Serbia must take place synchronisedly, as it will only give the expected effects. The second document is a bill confirming the Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Serbia and the Government of the Republic of Cyprus on co-operation in the field of maritime transport. I know the question of MPs will probably be why Serbia with Cyprus? Because Cyprus is the fourth largest ship in the world, and this agreement gives our sailors a chance to engage through Cyprus and work on those ships. So the Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Cyprus have not concluded an agreement on co-operation in maritime transport. Maritime transport is carried out in accordance with international conventions in the maritime areas which both countries have ratified. The conclusion of a maritime transport co-operation agreement between the Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Cyprus is a new concrete contribution to creating more favourable conditions for further improving bilateral economic co-operation between the two countries. The agreement is given importance to maritime transport, especially given that the Republic of Serbia has lost its seas since the decommissioning of the Serbia-Montenegro State Community, and that it has remained as a supersergist in all international conventions in the maritime area ratified by the former state. Given that maritime transport is one of the elements in the transport and supply of goods to the Republika Srpska market and given the economic and economic value of maritime transport compared to other modes of transport, there is a need for its strengthening and co-operation in this area with the Republic of Cyprus. The third document is the Proposal for a Law on Confirmation of the Strasbourg Convention on the Limitation of Liability in Internal Navigation. The Institute of responsibilities of shipowners is one of the basic principles of responsibility in maritime law and inland navigation rights and is one of the most important characteristics of this branch of law. In maritime law, the shipowner was always allowed to limit his responsibility to the value of maritime property involved in the disaster. Inland navigation, attempts were made to settle the issue through interstate instruments. The draft of an instrument made up by the EU Economic Commission for Europe, however, has never come into force. On the other hand, on the River Reyna it was adopted under the auspices of the Central Committee for the Sailing of the Paradise so-called "Rajna". The 1998 Strasbourg Convention on the Restriction of the responsibilities of shipowners of internal navigation. The States Parties to this Convention shall exclusively be the Rajean Middle States and that shall be Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Luxembourg. Since 1976, there has been no other attempt to adopt an appropriate international legal instrument that would uniquely regulate the Institute in the internal navigation across the European continent, the Central Commission for Navigation has launched an initiative to adopt amendments and additions to the Strasbourg Convention to extend it to the European level. Following the entry into force of the final text, a diplomatic conference in Strasbourg was scheduled for the working group of experts between 25 September and 27 September, which adopted the text of the Strasbourg Convention on the Restriction of Responsibility for Internal Navigation and the signing of the final diplomatic convention. Given that the Republic of Serbia is involved in a diplomatic conference as if it also signed the final act of the diplomatic convention, a process has been launched to confirm participants in the conference the adoption of the certification law. Thank you very much. ParlaMint-RS_2013-11-04-0.u25750	The President-in-Office, honourable ministers, esteemed colleagues, MPs and MPs, citizens of the Republic of Serbia, the SDPS parliamentary group supports the proposal for a Law on Railways because it believes that the solutions proposed are to the greatest extent possible, and that some parts of the professional public may be removed by amendments. In my presentation, I will not deal with all the many problems facing Serbia's railways, namely the state that covers their losses, but also citizens who are victims of unquality rail transport and who ultimately pay for all the wrong decisions made in the past in the rail transport sector. Regardless of the fact that each citizen of Serbia agrees with this claim, this is also the SDPS parliamentary group, and this problem is extremely serious, it is not the subject of today's debate, so I will leave it for another occasion, for example when some future budgets are passed in which we will be able to see the effects of this legal solution or of some colleagues who find it appropriate to talk about it today, which is their legitimate right. It is not rare to hear calls on Serbia's railways, as they call them the biggest losers in Serbia, while ignoring the fact that the system of rail traffic is systematic, unintended, but recklessly destroyed for years, so I would say even for decades, not entirely by market business, which has led it to the inability to generate free reproduction, about new investments that I don't even speak. When so unilaterally speaking about railways, and we know that it is much easier to criticise than something concrete to offer and do, it is too often forgotten that the comparative advantages of rail transport than other modes of transport, so I would remind fellow MPs and citizens that the railway has a far better option and greater efficiency of mass transport and goods and passengers than any other kind of traffic. The only one that is comparable is water transport in terms of price, but not in terms of speed. The railway has a far lower consumption of power than the mass of transport, or cargo, of about 40% of the consumption compared to road traffic, and a very approximate consumption of power from water traffic. There are far less negative environmental consequences. The cost of environmental traffic damage in the EU is about 4.6% of national income, of which 92% of road traffic, 7% is air traffic, and only 1.7% of rail traffic. It has far greater security than other traffic types compared to the number of people killed in traffic accidents for the same amount of transport. Between rail and road traffic is 1:100, and the damage is 1:3,500. Finally, the possibility of traffic taking place in almost all meteorological conditions, then the comfort of travel. Let's compare air transport and rail transport where there's no air transport between city centers, and there's a railroad. In airline transport it is impossible to use today inevitable electronic devices such as computers or mobile phones, and in railways it is. Not to mention the absence of waiting for boarding and landing which in the case of air traffic is something that spends a considerable amount of time, and that is not available in rail traffic. When we add to this the high speeds of transport that exist today, unfortunately not in all countries but in some EU countries, we see how many comparative advantages railways have on other modes of transport. Taking into account all the above, it is not difficult to conclude what kind of attention rail transport should have in every country that is strategically thinking and taking care of itself and its future. I believe that a good number of listed virtues of rail transport do not fully apply in our terms, but it is not a good part and a product of bad policymaking in recent decades. The mistakes of the past cannot be corrected overnight, but in order to correct them at all, it is necessary to take the first step, which is to create assumptions for the improvement of the Serbian Railway system. It is only possible to do so by passing a law that would respect the reality in which we live and in the given conditions to try to use the best applicable world practices, stressing the applicable ones, make all benefits of rail transport available to Serbian citizens. The bill of law that lies before us should not be seen as a final solution to all problems, far from it. He should be a good basis for an upgrade that could, unfortunately, at least on the mid-term, not so quickly, make the desired results. Unfortunately, in our old custom, with reforms and the passing of this law, we are quite late. For example, the deadline for the adoption of the reformed Railway Act expired approximately two years ago, according to the EU SAA and according to the information I received. To avoid misunderstandings, delay in the adoption of this law is not just a matter of EU association. It is much more a question of sustainability of the rail system in Serbia and the rest, not to say, survival in the European rail system. I doubt even the EU's most bitter opponents want the railway trip to any foreign country to become a nightmare for Serbian citizens. So the quickest adoption of this law is imperative. What are the most important innovations this law brings? The extension of the Railway Directorate's responsibilities, the adoption of a five-year national railway infrastructure programme, which will be adopted by the National Assembly on a proposal from the Government of Serbia, whose annual implementation will be supervised by the Government and reported to the Assembly, the removal in practice of the observed shortcomings of the previous legislative solution, the modernisation of the law and its adaptation to new EU directives and the removal of the provisions relating to the safety of rail traffic in the safety and interoperability of railways law. Although the Railways Directorate was established in 2004 and has since implemented its law of intended competence, it has shown in practice that its role should be far more significant, and this expects, for the truth, for the sake of will, that is to say, Brussels, and the EU. The existence and expansion of the Railway Directorate's intelligence is not something to worry about, because it is no new political trick for the recruitment of party personnel, but our obligation in the EU accession process. I will remind you that the Railways Directorate is the heiress of the Yugoslav Railways Community, so the bodies that existed 30 years before it, and for the sake of the unbelief of Tom, I will also say that, for example, The newly-roasted EU member Croatia has two agencies that are doing the same job at the moment, which will be entrusted to the Railway Directorate after the adoption of this law. So it's more economical than it's wasteful. In the absence of time, I will not enter all the new responsibilities of the Directorate, but instead, I will try to show the importance of expanding its powers on two illustrating examples. The first is that as of June 1st 2013, railway cars from Serbia will be able to cross Serbia's border with any other country only if they get a registration authorised by the Railways Directorate and with its new powers. So if we were not to pass this law by an emergency procedure, we would be put into a situation in order to have our cars stopped at borders on 1 June 2013. Another thing that is very important amongst the many new powers received by the Railways Directorate is that by adopting all the necessary standards and obtaining all the necessary certifications, we are opening new perspectives for our car industry, and we know in what state our car industry is and what problems we had in the previous period, especially some related to privatisation in this industry, which was once one of the feathers of our industry. So we are opening up new perspectives for it by being able to produce and remount cars for European railways, which is not possible at the moment. As far as the national railway infrastructure programme is concerned, it is a planned act of national importance in the railway area. It was about time, I dare say, that the solution to the problem of Serbian railways is approached strategically and that they are looking for systemic permanent solutions, instead of partial solutions, that is to do systematic, not ad hoc fire-fighting, and then by pushing the remaining unresolved problems under the carpet. A new concept of a railway organisation in Serbia, based on its division on two separate continents in rail traffic, should also be achieved, according to the minister, more efficient management of the railway system, but I would say a higher degree of transparency in the business of the Serbian Railways, both of which were not minor in the previous period. The obligation to separate infrastructures from the transport of goods and services, however, existed in the previous 2005 law, but was not fully defined, nor had an imperative tone. Now this is more precise and far more strictly defined, thus finally opening up the space for so much needed to introduce competition in railway transport. The expected effects of this measure are to reduce budget burdens based on the subsidisation of Serbia's Railways, but also to increase the quality of rail transport. In the future, all users, and by this I mean the Serbian Railways, but also some new operators, will pay for access to rail infrastructure, by subsidising the operation of the infrastructure manager, so the difference between the charges they have and the costs they have, which will probably be, even in some starting period, which can take longer, because its economic position, therefore, is unsustainable at this point. On the other hand, the public railway undertaking will no longer be obliged to retain all non-resistable lines, except those for which the state or body of local self-government is particularly interested, in which case they will be obliged to cover business losses on those lines. So we have an economic and marketable far better orderly situation. This will create the basis that, with the inevitable and urgent rationalisation of the business even if the domestic railway carrier, I am only talking about the work of the Serbian Railways, which, after its detachment, so to speak, is said to be different – spin of, exclusively by transporting passengers and goods, becoming a viable company in some future period. As for non-covered lines, they will be given a chance by some new interested operators, who may be able to deliver positive results with better business models. Of course, their right is not only limited to those lines that are not interested in Serbia's Railways, but also for other lines, which creates practically one system in which competition will strengthen, which will eventually create conditions for increasing the quality of rail traffic in Serbia. When we add to that the fact that, as I understand it, the Russian 800 million dollar loan is on the door, intended to improve the rail infrastructure in the most part, one part is for the purchase, as I understand it, twenty locomotives, but it is certainly a smaller part of that 800 million, and I would say that this is one of the first, if not the first serious investment in railways in the last few decades, then there is a reason for optimism, provided that the future rail system, or the entire rail traffic, is handled, as our people say, domestically. As for the provisions relating to the safety of rail transport, which have been removed from the Law on Railways in the Law on the Safety and Interoperability of Railways, which is still, unfortunately, not brought in, they almost create, I apologize for having to use perhaps too strong words, but I have received such information from some parts of the professional public, some kind of legal vacuum or interregne. The law which now regulates that area, which is thirty years old, has become obsolete in a partial conflict, has given me such information, with solutions from the new Railways Act, and the most urgent adoption of the law on safety and interoperability of railways is imposed as an imperative. To conclude, this Law on Railways is in this form which today is ahead of us cannot be considered an ideal solution, if such a solution even exists, I would dare even say long-term. I don't want this to cause me to panic with the people that there's going to be some new laws being passed all the time. Not to be misunderstood doesn't mean this bill is bad. On the contrary, the proposal is good because it represents a compromise of best European practices and our current real opportunities and capacities. The best confirmation of this is the positive criticism he received from the EU, regardless of what does not contain everything that is from us at the moment, I would say, unreally requested. Just copying an EU directive or a law from some of its members would be a dead letter on paper, as the Serbian Railway, as it is at the moment, is unable to face all the challenges that such legal solutions would put before it. This does not mean that to improve this legal solution through some future changes and additions, when conditions are acquired for such a thing, we should not work in the future. The first step is to adopt as soon as possible the safety and interoperability law of the railways, which, according to my information, as well as the minister can confirm whether they are correct, is expected within the next few months. To repeat, the SDPS parliamentary group considers the proposal for a railway law to be an improvement in earlier solutions, and will support it in this regard. Thank you. ParlaMint-RS_2013-11-04-0.u25774	The Honorable Chairman, Mr. Minister, members of the ministry, ladies and gentlemen of the People's Parliament, was passed in 2005 by a valid Railway Act. During the seven-year monitoring of the application of this law by the Ministry of Transport, as well as the application and analysis of the effects of the application of this law by the Railway Directorate, it has been established that it is necessary to access the adoption of a new law in order to effectively carry out operations in the area of rail traffic. Minister, we congratulate you on that. This is one of the first laws in this session that is comprehensive. We don't put out the fires and go to a whole new continent. The new draft law on railways sets out the harmonisation of the rules in the area of rail traffic with relevant EU regulations, I would like to say to the directives and regulations of the European railway community. I wouldn't count it all if I wasn't wasting my time. A decision to change the legal form of the Public Enterprise "The Railway of Serbia-Belgrade" was made before the law was drawn up. The decision is on amendments and additions to the founding act of the Public Enterprise "The Railway of Serbia". Those decisions have been reorganised by the Public Undertaking "The Railway of Serbia" on a completely new and modern basis in the Action Society "The Railway of Serbia", which allows for more efficient work and business in line with market conditions. The full application of that decision was not possible without the adoption of a new law governing rail traffic and creating the necessary environment for the operation and operation of that company. The government of the Republic of Serbia has agreed on a decision to organise the Action Society "Serb-Belgrade Railway" to comply with the Law on Business Society and Consent to the Statute of the Action Society "The Railway of Serbia". The lagging behind in harmonising the regulations of the Republic of Serbia, relating to rail traffic in relation to EU regulations, as well as the lagging behind in the restructuring of the said railway undertaking, i.e. the overall rail transport system in the territory of the Republic of Serbia, has already led to its incompatibility and discrepancies with the railways of the countries in the environment and with the railways of the EU countries. This led to a disproportion in investment in railways compared to road infrastructure. The railroad is falling short. The reason is that no investor wants to invest in an unrestructured, outdated and inefficient railway. Some of the consequences are already being felt, and this is bypassing Corridor 10 as the naturally most favourable and shortest road from Western Europe to Turkey and the Middle East and turning goods flows towards alternative routes across Romania and Bulgaria. As part of harmonising the RS rules with EU rules, as is done by this law, the results of the restructuring of railways that give the Republic of Serbia a great chance to educate efficient and effective rail traffic. Given that railways are a vital part of the state transport burden, the efficiency of the railway system should be improved in order to integrate this system into a competitive transport service market, as well as that rail traffic should be made more efficient and more competitive than other modes of traffic. It is necessary that the State enables railway undertakings to be independent operators to operate in a commercial manner in accordance with market requirements. The future development and efficient operation of the railway system can be improved if there is a difference between the provision of transport services on the one hand and the management of infrastructure on the other hand, with the need to manage this concept with these two activities and that they have their own accounts, as provided for in this law. It's a very important item. One of the main objectives of rail development through restructuring is that when competition does come, these railway companies are in a strong position to survive on the market. The new Law on Railways also modernises specific parts of the laws governing access and use of railway infrastructure in order to achieve competition with regard to the provision of services to rail users in terms of improving comforts and services in general. The State retains responsibility for the development of adequate railway infrastructure. The infrastructure manager, with the consent of the Government, is required to establish rules governing the fees and prices of railway service providers for the use of railway infrastructure. The state should provide a sound financial structure, especially for an existing state-owned railway carrier. The significant paper provided for in this law refers to the introduction of a national railway infrastructure programme, which brings the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia to the government's proposal. This national programme is a planned act of national importance in the railway area. The solutions provided for in this bill will have a positive impact on all participants in the rail traffic process, the Railways and Business Directorate of the Republic of Serbia, and therefore the PUPS parliamentary group will support this law with improvements that will take place through a debate in principle and in particular, expressed in the amendments.
