ParlaMint-RS_2013-11-04-0.u25900	Mr. President, Mr. Minister, distinguished colleagues, respected citizens of Serbia, at the beginning of my presentation, I would like to express my satisfaction on behalf of the NS parliamentary group, which is a large number of essential amendments, which the NS parliamentary group has submitted in the previous term, included in this law, so that in one indirect way we also consider us as people who participated in the creation of this law. There has been no change to the Law on Railways since 2005. This law is seen as a law which aims to improve the capacity of the railway system and this law, in our deep opinion, creates conditions for the independent business of railway undertakings, with increased competitiveness and improved quality of rail transport in general. I also consider a good provision of this law that the separation of the rail system must in some way be done by detachment for the steering part when it comes to infrastructure and the part responsible for transport in passenger and freight traffic. In my deep opinion, this law also has two very precise solutions when it comes to intermodal, combined traffic, but also the competences of the Railway Directorate, which are very precisely defined by this law. When it comes to combined transport, I believe that Article 83 is very clear in order to improve combined transport that the government is regulating this area and very clear state aid and stimulating measures, and when we recently discussed the Energy Efficiency Act, we pointed out the advantages of combined traffic and many colleagues pointed out that just combined traffic is cleaner, that we have very little pollution and it is very important to define this traffic precisely and further improve it. As for the Directorate, the big problem so far has been that the powers of the Directorate have not been correctly specified, in the sense that the Directorate could not bring in sublegal acts, and the jurisdiction of the Railway Directorate has been very clearly specified and, as you, Mr Minister, said, the Directorate is now a body for licensing and the regulatory body and security. I would also agree with my colleague, Baure, who said this law for the first time clearly provides that the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia adopts a national railway infrastructure programme on a proposal from the government. In this way we clearly have a national programme involving the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia and the Government of the Republic of Serbia. The problem of the previous law was that it was not in line with EU law and was also a problem that was not applied in practice and unfortunately, with the restructuring in railways under the previous law did not continue. The direct consequence of this was disproportionate investment in railways and road traffic. So more has been invested in road traffic. Again, the question arises – who should invest in unrestructured and inefficient railways? As a consequence, we had railway transport, instead of Corridor 10, as naturally the most suitable and shortest route from Western Europe to Turkey and the Middle East, taking alternative routes across Romania to Bulgaria. The new law harmonizes all its solutions with the EU legal framework and, regardless of the fact that in Western European countries, the market share in most railways began to decline in the 50s as a result of the transition of the economy from a traditionally difficult industry to the service and retail industry, however, these legal solutions in EU countries have produced some results. I think it is clear to all of us that the Serbian Railways in this form cannot withstand a competition that will certainly emerge as a result of the adoption of this law and therefore a fundamental reorganisation of this public enterprise is necessary. Given that the Railway is a vital part of the transport sector, I consider it to be a very important provision of this law that will allow railway operators to be granted the status of independent operators. In this way, they will operate on a commercial basis and in line with market requirements. The future development and efficient functioning of the railway system can only be improved if the difference between the provision of transport services and infrastructure management is made. Regardless of the incentive of competitiveness, I consider it very responsible that the state remains responsible for the development of railway infrastructure, and the law defines that the infrastructure manager, with the consent of the Government, is obliged to establish the rules governing both the fees and prices of railway undertakings' services for the use of railway infrastructure, which must respect the principle of non-discrimination between railway undertakings. This law also provides for incentives to manage railway infrastructures, to reduce costs and to manage rail infrastructure as efficiently as possible, and in this respect I believe that certain contracts to be signed between local self-governments and the previous provinces and government will produce some results in terms of reducing the cost of rail infrastructure management. I believe that these revenues, which will thus be achieved, will significantly reduce the subsidies that the state of Serbia is currently giving for the railway, which, as a direct positive objective of this law, will have to disburse the budget. This law regulates the public transport obligation of passengers in a way that is regulated by European countries, and these legal solutions are more precise and efficient than traditional state aid to ensure smooth public transport of passengers. In order for public transport of passengers to be organised in a way that meets the needs of the public, the competent authorities must have the option of free choice of rail transport. In order to guarantee the application of the principle of transparency as well as the equal treatment of competing railway undertakings, it is essential that the public transport obligation contract, between the competent authority and the selected railway undertaking, defines the nature of the public transport obligation, as well as the agreed compensation. All in all, I believe that these solutions should lead to an increase in interest in rail traffic, both in the country itself and in countries associated with the railway infrastructure with Serbia. I believe these changes of law will attract foreign investors who will have a positive effect on the economy and citizens in general. That is why the NS parliamentary group will support this law in the voting day. Thank you. ParlaMint-RS_2013-11-04-0.u26042	The Honored Chairman, distinguished colleagues and fellow Members of Parliament and MPs, respected citizens of the proposed amendment should not be accepted for three basic reasons. The first reason why the amendment should not be accepted is to prevent equal access to justice. This is reflected in the fact that the amendment promoter treats state-owned enterprises and private enterprises in a completely different way, i.e. private enterprises, or companies with majority private capital, is given the opportunity to choose their own contractors. The aim of the legislator and the general objective of the SNS is for all to be equal before the law, not for individuals or individual companies to be favored in any way by private or state. So that's the first reason this amendment should be rejected. The second reason why this amendment should be refused is to compromise the principle of efficiency which is both important and significant in the enforcement process. And how does the amendment's proposing compromise this principle of efficiency? It endangers it by giving the chamber 15 days to respond upon request again and giving the chamber authority to verify whether the debtor has settled his obligations before the court even though we know well that the check is the previous question and that it has already been resolved, and that the check has already been carried out. Therefore, for reasons of jeopardising equal access to justice to all the factors of this society, for the purpose of jeopardising efficiency, for the purpose of jeopardising economics, this amendment is not acceptable to the SNS. ParlaMint-RS_2013-11-04-0.u26080	The President-in-Office, Mr. Minister, ladies and gentlemen of the People's Parliament, aims to improve and make the rail system of the Republic of Serbia effective and integrate Serbian railways into EU rail systems. During the five-year follow-up period, many shortcomings in the current Railway Act have been observed. The lack of a valid railway law has been found by the Ministry of Traffic and Railway Directorates. In the course of law enforcement, shortcomings have been identified that required compliance with the new packages of the EU Directive, as well as the extension of the railway section. The Railway Directorate did not have the right under the existing law to submit sublegal acts adopted under the Law on the Safety of Railway Traffic, although they are necessary for the safe conduct of rail traffic. The new draft law on railways as one of many objectives has exactly the aim of harmonising the law with the draft law on the safety and interoperability of railways that is done in parallel with this law. Special attention to the new law is given to the regulation of combined transport i.e. transport where most of the road is carried out by rail services. Despite this importance and potential, this part has been ignored by the current Law on Railways. In particular, the proposal for a railway law highlights the significant achievement and precision of the part of the law governing access to rail infrastructure and its improvement. Another newspaper envisioned by the new railway law is the introduction of a national railway infrastructure programme, which brings the National Assembly of RS to the government's proposal and represents an act of national importance in the railway area. The new law also envisions the realisation of railway infrastructure that was neglected during the previous period due to the weakened economy and the country's economy. The new law also provides for the rights and means of giving to the management of railway infrastructure. The new laws create conditions for several railway undertakings and railway infrastructure managers, which should lead to competition and increased transport quality in rail transport. The new law obliges the state to provide a sound financial structure, especially on existing rail transport that is state-owned and represents the national interest of the state. Several working subgroups were formed during the construction of a new law at different stages, consisting of representatives of the most significant stakeholders, which are related to the area of rail traffic, such as the Railway Directorate, the AD Railway of Serbia, the company for the construction of the railway node "Belgrade" DOO, the Faculty of Transport and the tweening consultant and experts from the French and Lithuanian transport ministries. Public debates were held on the draft of the railway law, so that all interested entities could deliver their suggestions and objections to this law. The draft law on railways was published on the Ministry's website for traffic operations. This is where suggestions and comments were provided by individual sectors of "Serb Railways" AD, which concerned the protection of railway infrastructure and the application of the law governing public property. The province's secretariat for the economy and employment of the AP Vojvodina addressed under this law to the AP Vojvodina. The new railway law has also been approved by the European Commission's competent authorities, whose proposals and suggestions have been accepted in the most part and this has led to a positive opinion from the European Integration Office. Finally, the adoption of this law by emergency procedure by the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia is necessary for a reason because the failure to pass this law by emergency procedure would lead to significant adverse consequences for rail traffic and railway infrastructure in RS, as well as for the overall economy of the Republic of Serbia. For this reason, the SNS parliamentary group in the voting day will vote on this proposal.
